key_insight: This review finds that operations research in elderly care has advanced from fixed routing and scheduling toward dynamic, AI-enabled decision support, but it still often stops at operational efficiency rather than improving patient outcomes.
clinical_relevance: For health systems, the most important takeaway is that better workforce and care-process planning may help older adults only if these tools are integrated with clinical, community, and transition-of-care decisions.
method: The authors reviewed 30 seminal studies at the intersection of industrial engineering, operations research, and elderly care.
They grouped the literature into three themes: home healthcare operations, polypharmacy management, and clinical chronotherapy.
They compared modeling trends over time, highlighting a shift from deterministic methods to stochastic and AI-assisted approaches.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a thematic review of 30 studies, showing a clear methodological evolution but limited evidence that operational gains translate into measurable clinical outcomes.
watch_item: A major limitation is the translational gap: many models optimize logistics well, but are not yet validated for real-world patient health impact or for hospital-to-community care transitions.
paper_title: From Operations to Elderly Care Outcomes: A Thematic Review of Industrial Engineering and Decision-Support Approaches
